name: BLINK
intro: BLINK是一个针对多模态大语言模型（LLMs）的新基准，专注于其他评估中未发现的核心视觉感知能力。它将14个经典的计算机视觉任务重新格式化为3,807个多项选择题，并配有单张或多张图像和视觉提示。BLINK旨在刺激社区帮助多模态LLMs赶上人类水平的视觉感知。
org: University of Pennsylvania, University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI, University of California Davis, Columbia University
build_method: 经典视觉任务改写、既有数据集复用、新数据采集、人工去歧义质检
build_method_en: Classic-Vision Task Recasting, Dataset Reuse, New Data Collection, Manual Ambiguity Review
eval_feature_en: Zero-Shot, Visual Prompting, Single/Multi-Image, Human and Specialist Baselines
intro_en: BLINK is a new benchmark for multimodal large language models (LLMs) that focuses on core visual perception abilities not captured by other evaluations. It reformats 14 classic computer vision tasks into 3,807 multiple-choice questions, accompanied by single or multiple images and visual prompts. BLINK aims to encourage the community to help multimodal LLMs reach human-level visual perception.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2404.12390v4 §3.2, §4.1, and Appendix A. Primary release evidence is official repo 529b0ba055416dea5df79d594e7f62a910d8a308 plus HF dataset revision a3666eb249237ba3d5eca8db21176cc47967e040; repository locators are README.md, eval/test_benchmark.py, eval/multiple_choice.py, eval/query_model.py, eval/evaluate.py, and eval/README.md. The paper and pinned HF data define the canonical 3,807 questions as 1,901 validation plus 1,906 test over 7,358 images, while the pinned repository README separately reports 1,907 test questions; the official sources do not explain the difference, so it is preserved without assigning a cause. The build chain reuses 12 named vision sources, creates SDXL-versus-matched-real-photo forensics and license-friendly IQ items, recasts 14 tasks as MCQs with visual prompts, enforces unique images and manual ambiguity removal, and evaluates without resizing at temperature 0 with up to 10 retries. Choice extraction uses predefined rules followed by GPT-3.5-Turbo fallback; reporting uses per-task accuracy and a 14-task macro average, with human, caption-only, prompt-sensitivity, random, MLLM, and specialist comparisons.
